root_idea.summary: The root centers on making something exposed, especially an ugly fault, and also denotes an unattractive or mixed pale color.
root_idea.development: The exposure branch includes becoming visible, bringing faults into public shame, and figuratively outshining something until it is no longer distinct. A parallel color branch covers pale or grayish hues, redness appearing in dates, and color-based names for certain animals.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole supplied Quran-attested group is displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To expose a person's faults, disgrace the person, or put the person to shame.
senses.usage_conditions: Used transitively for making vices, faults, or evil conduct public, especially before other people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To outshine or eclipse another thing so that it is no longer apparent or distinct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use, especially of the moon or dawn overpowering the light of the stars.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of dawn or daybreak, to break forth and shine, making what it overtakes visible or exposed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dawn-related use describing either the revealing light of daybreak or its sudden coming upon someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become of the pale or mixed color called فُضْحَةٌ.
To expose or disgrace one another by each revealing the other's faults.
Of unripe dates or palm trees, to show redness or become red and yellow in the fruit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the visible development of color in dates and palms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To expose one another's faults or disgrace one another.
For one's faults or evil qualities to become exposed; to become disgraced or put to shame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive or middle-result construction, including becoming disgraced through one's own wrongdoing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiomatic use, to fail in one's duty toward someone by neglecting to visit or seek that person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression of regret for negligence in maintaining contact or offering attention.
A nominal description of the reddish appearance of dawn, associated with its shining forth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pale, whitish, dusty-gray, or otherwise unattractively mixed color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of colors of camels and pigeons; the whiteness of dawn may also be called فُضْحَةُ الصُّبْحِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who habitually or frequently exposes the faults and evil qualities of others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive or habitual agent noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person made notorious by evil character or conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in a vocative expression addressing such a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bad manager of property or cattle, one who does not take proper care of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of negligent management.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Disgrace, shame, or ignominy; a state of exposure of faults, or anything disgraceful that exposes its author to shame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract noun covering the condition, the act, or the shameful fault or thing itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who exposes or disgraces others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active participle of the transitive Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dawn or daybreak, as that which exposes and makes everything manifest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative nominal use based on the revealing effect of daylight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pale or lightly white, without intense whiteness; also a lion or camel designated by such coloration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal designations are based on the coloration associated with this adjective.

cautions: The Quran occurrence is the active imperfect form تَفْضَحُ; the public headword is normalized to the Form I perfect فَضَحَ. The dawn and color branches are retained as broader Classical Arabic usages rather than merged into the Quranic disgrace sense.
